conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Strange Attractor
style.description: The Lorenz butterfly as a glossy wire sculpture in a bright studio: each path is a thick lacquered tube (coral, teal) with a glowing bead at its head, drawn as the last few seconds of the path, over a pale floor that catches its soft shadow. Paths are integrated once at load (lorenz.js, fixed-step RK4) and read back by time; two starts a hair apart run as one twisted two-colour strand until they part at a fork, and a speck of 200 beads bursts across both wings. A small unlabelled dial shows the gap between the two beads.
motion: Every path is integrated once at load (fixed-step RK4) and read back by t: the tube is the last few tau of the path up to now.
Two starts a hair apart share one twisted two-colour strand while the twin stays on the coral's path; it opens for good at the fork.
The cloud: 200 starts packed into a speck at the fork, released together, spread across both wings.
Camera: one move per beat; the fork shot faces the split so one bead goes left and one right.

beats.label: A twin starts a hair apart
